title: Normalization, Orthographic Regularization & TEI Primary Sources
query: How should orthographic variation such as iotacism be normalized in historical manuscripts, and how do rule-based scripts and AI models compare when encoding TEI orig and reg elements?

results.authors_venue_year: [PDF][PDF] Resolving High-Vowel Ambiguity (⟨ ï⟩/⟨ i⟩/⟨ ı⟩) in OCR-Derived Old Turkic Editions: An Edition-Metadata-Driven Disambiguation LayerE Uçar - Turkic Studies Journal, 2026 - pdfs.semanticscholar.orgProposes a dedicated disambiguation layer integrated into a TEI-P5 two-layer encoding framework (orig/reg) to handle orthographic variation, operating at the graphemic representation level using edition-specific metadata and rule-based linguistic cues.Handling Ambiguity: Explains that orthographic variation such as high-vowel collapse is a main error type that cannot be resolved solely at the representation level, and the proposed method successfully disambiguates approximately 88–93% of high-vowel ambiguity cases while preserving unresolved forms through explicit TEI `<unclear>` annotation.Deterministic Normalization: Uses a deterministic system of priority and avoids probabilistic methods, prioritizing philological verifiability over statistical generalization for text normalization.Save Cite Related articles All 2 versions  No full text available View as HTML [PDF] aclanthology.org

results.title: A large-scale comparison of historical text normalization systems
results.authors_venue_year: A large-scale comparison of historical text normalization systemsM Bollmann - Proceedings of the 2019 conference of the north …, 2019 - aclanthology.orgReviews existing literature and reports experiments comparing systems spanning all categories of proposed normalization techniques, including rule-based methods, distance metrics, statistical machine translation, and neural encoder–decoder models, across eight languages.Normalization Approaches: Outlines normalization techniques that include hand-crafted algorithms tailored to specific languages, supervised machine learning, character-based statistical machine translation (SMT), and neural machine translation (NMT).Definition of Normalization: Defines historical text normalization as mapping historical variant spellings to a single, contemporary “normal form” to address spelling variation challenges in historical NLP.Save Cite Cited by 137 Related articles All 8 versions  No full text available View as HTML

results.title: The identification of spelling variants in English and German historical texts: Manual or automatic?
results.authors_venue_year: The identification of spelling variants in English and German historical texts: Manual or automatic?T Pilz, A Ernst-Gerlach, S Kempken… - Literary and …, 2008 - academic.oup.comDiscusses two approaches for addressing spelling variation in historical German and English texts: one aiming to develop a search engine and the other aiming to improve corpus linguistic techniques, both sharing a goal of assessing a generic spelling detection tool for Indo-European languages.Normalizing Variants with VARD: Explains that the VARD tool for English historical texts uses a list of variant forms and their modern equivalents to insert a modern form alongside the historical variant, preserved using an XML 'reg' tag, to detect and normalize spelling variants.Comparing Manual and Automatic Rules: Compares manual rule derivation, trained string edit distance, and automatic rule learning as three different paths taken by the German RSNSR project to reach its goal of reliable full text-searches in historical documents with non-standard orthography.Save Cite Cited by 43 Related articles All 10 versions  No full text available [PDF] semanticscholar.org

results.title: The role of error in the computational generation of word forms
results.authors_venue_year: [PDF][PDF] The role of error in the computational generation of word formsT Mező - Journal of Advanced Artificial Intelligence and Machine …, 2025 - scivisionpub.comApplies a hybrid processing pipeline that includes neural HTR-based correction (Transformer+CTC), a rule-based finite-state transducer (FST) for stem and affix normalization, and edit distance with trigram language model fine-tuning to address orthographic fluctuations and scribal errors.Modeling Orthographic Variation: Models and corrects orthographic phenomena by integrating neural HTR with rule-based FST and a noisy channel model, treating errors as reconstructible historical markers rather than simple noise.TEI Encoding Comparison: Mentions that the Medieval Nordic Text Archive (MENOTA) uses the TEI P5 standard, applying the `<allomorph>` tag to mark stem and suffix alternations, and performs normalization using FST, illustrating a comparison of rule-based scripts in encoding TEI elements.Save Cite Cited by 1 Related articles All 2 versions  View as HTML [PDF] birmingham.ac.uk
